Janjgir-Champa, Chhattisgarh ---- Respondents
For Petitioners : Mr. N.K. Chatterjee, Advocate For State : Mr. Lav Sharma, Panel Lawyer Hon'ble
Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey Order on Board 04.04.2025
1.

The petitioners have filed this petition seeking the following relief(s):-
"10.1

This Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondents to grant compensation for the land bearing Khasra No.176/2/M/1, 2, 3 (total 0.64 acres) of the land of petitioners from the date of acquisition and also grant the interest @ 18 p.a..

10.2 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondents to calculate the compensation as per the present market value and as per the nature of land, which has not been properly calculated."

10.3 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to calculate compensation in the light of Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10.4 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash the impugned letter dated 18-04-2019 (Annexure P-4).

10.5 Any appropriate writ, direction or order may also kindly be passed in favour of the petitioners,
which this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the circumstances of the case."
2.

Mr. Chatterjee, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the Land Acquisition Officer has not awarded adequate compensation according to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013') as per market value.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
He would further submit that the objection raised by the petitioners was rejected vide order dated 08.01.2014 by the Land Acquisition Officer without assigning sufficient reason.
3.
On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State would oppose the submissions made by Mr. Chatterjee.

He would submit that Survey No.176/2/M/2 & 3, total area of 0.64 acres situated at Taga, Patwari Circle No.18, Tahsil Akaltara, District Janjgir-Champa (C.G.) was acquired and an award was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
He would further submit that a reference was made by the petitioners before the Tribunal and it was decided vide order dated 18.04.2019.
He would contend that the entire land of the petitioners admeasuring 0.64 acres was acquired and adequate compensation was paid with interest and solatium.

He would further argue that the Vishal Nath Sahu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35926717/
2 compensation was assessed according to the market value.

entities.text: Vishal Nath Sahu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Mr. Sharma would also argue that the objection raised by the petitioners was rejected on 08.01.2014 and thereafter, an award was passed and the reference has also been decided by the learned Tribunal vide order dated 18.04.2019.
4.
I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the documents placed on the record.

5. Taking into consideration the fact that the entire land of the petitioners admeasuring 0.64 acres was acquired and compensation was paid and thus, the relief sought in para 10.1 has already been redressed.

The compensation was assessed according to the provisions of the Act of 2013 and thus,
no case is made out to grant relief clause 10.3.
6. The objection of the petitioners was rejected on 08.01.2014 and in relief clause 10.4, the petitioners have given incorrect date of the order whereby the objection was rejected.
As the objection raised by the petitioners was already decided, no direction can be issued to the respondent authorities to decide the objection again.
7. Taking into consideration the above-discussed facts, no case is made out for interference.
Accordingly, the present petition is dismissed.
However, the petitioners would be at liberty to take recourse to law, if so advised.
